items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: This Eddie that played trombone with him... Eddie Marsh... I worked with Rene... They have a pretty good band... Eddie, trombone player

ctx.x: kid Rene? Did you ever know him? Oh yeah. I worked often and on when Joe was sick or he had two jobs. I worked with Rene, Kid Rene. They have a pretty good band? Yeah, yeah. Great band. And they had one of the top bands. Who was in it? Well Eddie, trombone player, Peter Pappy, playing clarinet. Peter Pappy playing banjo, Zeb. Johnny Prydoch playing bass at the time when I played with him. That'd be a band. Unless they had saxophone. He did. Manny Gabriel, he was playing saxophone. Violin? Have any violins? No, he…

did he live? Oh Eddie Marsh. Eddie Marsh, he's still alive. Yeah. I think Eddie lives, I don't know, somewhere about. Oh yeah, St. Phillip. Yeah, up there. I just wondered if it was the same guy. Yeah, that's him. That looks like about the end of this reel. This is real. See, this is real too, Albert Giles. February the 24th, 1961. What kind of

jobs would a band like Rene play? Well he played advertisements, Sunday dances for clubs at home, and then he played clubs. Halls like the Corporators, Economy Hall, the Poitier Hall, the Jean-Amé Hall, the Fethian Tempher, all those old dance halls at that time. They had clubs mostly give dances, and you found men sponsored dances of their own and they charge admission. But they all had advertisements. The dances mostly was on Sunday night and Monday nights for colored people. And they would advertise and you…
